text:
alex: quick check — ran a dry run of the SCIM sync for contractor groups and noticed deprovisioning shows as a deferred job (approx 10m delay). can we make deprov immediate for groups with prefix `contractor-`?

mira: do you mean immediate deletion or just disabling SSO/login? we usually soft-delete for 24h to allow reassignments.

alex: for legal/compliance the customer asked for faster offboarding for contractors. immediate disable + anonymize email in logs should be fine. not trying to resurrect users, just ensure access cut ASAP.

devon: short answer: we have a flag `deprov_mode` on the scim-group mapping that currently defaults to `delayed`. changing to `immediate` is straightforward but we need to handle collisions where a user is in both contractor and full-time groups. do we want priority rules?

sam: +1 on priority rules. maybe rule: explicit employee groups win over contractor groups, unless group has `force_deprov=true` tag.

alex: good point — proposed rule: if user is in any `employee-*` group, do not auto-deprov from `contractor-*`. if only contractor groups, immediate.

ops-sre: note: our audit logs currently include `user.email` in SCIM events. if we immediately deprov+delete, we need to redact email from long-term logs per privacy policy. otherwise PII retention policy is violated.

mira: agreed. we should redact `user.email` in log messages and keep only hashed id for audit. do we have a PR for the log redaction change?

security-bot: auto-check: GDPR retention policy flagged. Recommend add `redact_pii=true` to scim-sync config for deprov flows.

alex: here's what I ran locally: `./scim-sync --group-prefix contractor- --dry-run`. sample PATCH we use to remove member:```json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {
      "op": "Remove",
      "path": "members[value eq \"user-id-123\"]"
    }
  ]
}
```

devon: for the collisions we can add evaluation order: `employee-*` (highest), `contractor-force` (next), `contractor-*` (lowest). implementable in mapping table + unit tests.

sam: i'll draft the mapping table and tests. can someone +1 on changing live config? we should rollout to staging first.

tara: i can do staging deploy and watch the sync logs. i'll also add a redaction middleware so SCIM events emitted to long-term bucket replace emails with `<<redacted>>` and include `email_hash`.

alex: sounds good. action items: 1) sam to open mapping + config PR, 2) tara adds redaction middleware and staging deploy, 3) devon adds priority logic + tests, 4) ops-sre to validate no backup jobs rely on raw email after deletion. i'll open the GH PR link once sam starts.

sam: opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3421 — includes mapping table change and a config flag `deprov_mode: immediate` for `contractor-*` patterns. requesting reviews from @devon @mira @ops-sre.

devon: reading PR now. quick note: add a test for a user in both `employee-core` and `contractor-temp` to assert employee wins.

ops-sre: i'll check downstream systems (backup indexing, analytics pipelines) tonight. flagging potential follow-up if any pipeline expects `user.email` to join events.

mira: once PR is ready, can we also add a short runbook entry for oncall describing how to revert mapping toggles if we see mass undesired deprovs? (last time we had a mapping bug it hit 3 tenants).

alex: yes, i'll draft the runbook snippet and add to the PR description.

security-bot: reminder: any change that affects deprovisioning must go through privileged-access review. tag `security-review` on the PR.

sam: tagged `security-review` and added changelog; pinging reviewers.

alex: thanks — once staged and redaction verified, we'll flip `deprov_mode` for contractor groups. small heads-up to support: i'll post a short note to #support about expected behavior during rollout. :thumbsup:

mira: thanks all.
